Apple's brand-new M6 Mac mini, M5 Pro mini, and Mac Studio go on sale tomorrow. Although most models already have early bird pre-order discounts, let's first take a look at some of our favourite Mac accessories today.

Essential Mac mini/Studio Accessories Recommendations

If you ask me, the best accessories for the Mac mini or Mac Studio are definitely Apple's Magic Keyboard, Magic Mouse, and Studio Display. Of course, some people hate the Magic Mouse (they're wrong, because gesture controls are essential and revolutionary), but I do admit the keyboard has room for improvement, and the Magic Mouse isn't ergonomic enough for some people... I understand.

With that said, let's jump right into our top picks. Besides Apple's own products, there are plenty of third-party accessories we use ourselves:

Justin – Apple Studio Display

Let's start with the display—you need a monitor. If you haven't bought one yet or are thinking of upgrading, you can now grab the most affordable Studio Display from Apple's website at the lowest discount ever, taking $240 off (while stocks last), so I've included it in today's recommendations.

I personally use a Samsung Smart Monitor with my Mac mini. The M9 OLED model isn't cheap, but it perfectly matches the Mac mini's Apple aesthetic (the silver finish looks almost like an iMac), and it's a few hundred dollars cheaper than the Studio Display. At 32 inches, it has built-in streaming capabilities and plenty of other selling points. Of course, there are many other options on the market, some even more affordable, so I asked my colleagues to share their recommendations and introduce the screens they use every day:

  • Buy the ASUS ProArt (PA27JCV) 27-inch 5K USB-C Monitor
  • Buy the Samsung 32-inch OLED M9 Smart Monitor
  • Buy the Dell UltraSharp 27 Thunderbolt Hub Monitor
  • Buy the LG 27UP850K-W 27-inch Ultrafine 4K Monitor
  • Buy the LG 32-inch UltraFine 6K Thunderbolt 5 Monitor
  • Buy the BenQ PD2730S 27-inch 5K Thunderbolt 4 Monitor
  • Buy the ASUS 32-inch ProArt 6K Monitor

Chance – Logitech MX Master 4

If you've bought a new Mac mini or Mac Studio, you'll need to get your own peripherals. My top mouse pick is the Logitech MX Master 4. It offers several new features over the previous generation, including haptic feedback, better connectivity, and more durable, comfortable materials. Logitech has retained the classic elements of the MX Master 3 while making excellent modern improvements.

As a secondary recommendation, if you're looking for a mouse with a different ergonomic design, the Logitech MX Vertical is also a solid choice.

Michael – Satechi Hub & Stand with NVMe SSD Enclosure for Mac mini or Mac Studio

The Satechi Mac mini Hub & Stand is a simple and convenient way to add more storage and ports to your Mac mini. It has a built-in NVMe SSD enclosure, allowing you to easily add affordable extra storage without opening up your Mac mini. It also doubles as a USB hub, with convenient front-facing USB ports and an SD card reader for connecting peripherals or transferring photos and videos. Installation is straightforward, and the whole thing sits neatly beneath your new Mac mini.

If you've chosen the Mac Studio instead of the Mac mini, Satechi also offers a Hub & Stand designed specifically for the Mac Studio.

Simon – Silkland Right-Angle 240W Thunderbolt 5 Cable

A new Mac mini or Mac Studio looks great on your desk—until you see all the cables. That's why I recommend using right-angle cables like these. If you place your new Mac at the edge of your desk, the cables can run straight down without protruding. It supports charging speeds of up to 240W and bandwidth of 120Gbps. This Thunderbolt 5 cable comes in various lengths, starting at $26.

If you find the HDMI ports on the back of your Mac desktop insufficient, you might also want to grab a 10-foot USB-C to HDMI cable for under $14.

Karthik – Satechi SM1 75% Mechanical Keyboard

A Mac mini must be paired with a keyboard. If you're planning to buy a new one, I'd go with the Satechi SM1 75% Mechanical Keyboard. Its compact layout keeps things tidy while retaining practical keys like the function row and arrow keys, and the mechanical switches provide a more satisfying typing feel than typical low-profile keyboards. The light grey and white colourway looks great next to the Mac mini, making it ideal for those who love a clean Apple-style desk setup.

If you prefer a thinner, quieter wireless keyboard suited for office use, consider the Keychron B1 Pro, which features a silent scissor-switch design.

Rein – Insta360 Link 2 Pro 4K PTZ Webcam

You might pair your Mac mini or Mac Studio with an Apple display, which already has a built-in camera. But if not, you should check out Insta360's models. I therefore recommend the Insta360 Link 2 Pro 4K PTZ Webcam or one of its other variants. You get sharper 4K resolution, dual microphones with beamforming, AI-powered smart tracking, and compatibility with various video conferencing software, streaming platforms, and Stream Deck integration.

  • Buy the Insta360 Link 2 Pro 4K PTZ Webcam
  • Buy the Insta360 Link 2C Pro 4K Webcam
  • Buy the Insta360 Link 2 4K PTZ Webcam
  • Buy the Insta360 Link 2C 4K Webcam

Secondary Recommendations

  • Logitech MX Keys S Mac Wireless Keyboard
  • Satechi Thunderbolt 5 CubeDock
  • HyperDrive Next Thunderbolt 5 Dock with SSD Enclosure
  • Anker Prime Thunderbolt 5 Dock
  • Latest Apple Magic Keyboard
  • Latest Apple Magic Mouse
